headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad networked scraping can leak or cascade untrusted web content into downstream workflows, while the awesome-list profile adds no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B’s outputs. Profile B has broad network egress and MCP-compatible client support, meaning it can fetch attacker-controlled web content that could be copied into A’s downstream workflows if the pair is manually bridged. The interaction is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B fetches untrusted web pages and an operator forwards that content into A-linked workflows, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF A is used as a manual reference source for B without content filtering, injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy with content sanitization.
Strip scripts and hidden text from scraped pages before reuse.
Add a short human review step for any web-derived instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to scraped content.
requires-engineering: isolate B’s fetched content from any instruction channel into A.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B handles web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, and can send data to external APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or operator workflow, B can expose sensitive material from its context while A provides no containment. This is a default-risk pathway for B, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or clipboard, B’s screenshots or API-key-bearing context can be exposed outside the intended boundary.
IF B is pointed at pages containing secrets or credentials, its broad egress can transmit them to third parties.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B’s scrape targets.
Rotate any API keys used by B on a short schedule.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.
requires-engineering: disable external egress for sensitive runs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or runtime surfaces, so it cannot materially contend for shared mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and has API/CLI surfaces, but the profile does not show shared filesystem writes or git/database mutation. The plausible conflict is limited to unusual orchestration, so low is sufficient.
conditions: IF an operator wires both agents to the same mutable workspace, write conflicts can occur.
IF B instances are pointed at the same external API quota or secret, contention may arise.
mitigations: Assign separate API keys per instance.
Use distinct working directories.
Serialize any shared external writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent quota partitioning.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a crawler/extractor with broad egress and markdown-oriented outputs, so its results can be treated as authoritative downstream. A provides no verification or critique mechanism, and nothing in either profile shows a guardrail that would stop B from acting on A-derived content. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the blast radius is bounded by the operator’s use of the outputs.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated summaries or facts without verification, downstream actions can be based on errors.
IF A is used to curate sources for B, B may propagate mistaken or stale content into outputs.
mitigations: Require a human check before any action based on B’s output.
Compare B’s output against the original source page.
Limit B to extraction, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks.
requires-engineering: block autonomous side effects from B outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles API keys and broad web content, which can create retention and residency issues if regulated data is scraped or stored. A is an open-source docs-only list with no touched data classes, so it is not the compliance driver here. Because the mismatch is driven by B’s handling of sensitive inputs and external APIs, medium is the right level.
conditions: IF B processes regulated personal data or secrets, its external API use can create retention or residency obligations.
IF scraped content includes jurisdictional personal data, compliance controls must be applied before storage or forwarding.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Review B’s retention settings before use.
Separate EU and US data flows.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows for stored scrape artifacts.
